title: Usage integrity
description: LLM usage shipped to HAR HQ is counted exactly once and where it happened. Each station adds a question the gate keeps asking: do the usage invariants (I1-I5) catch every shape the usage audit found, and does the real path — OTLP into Mission Control, attribution, har control sync — ship usage that keeps them.

stations.title: The invariants catch every audited shape
stations.description: One pure definition of right usage (@har/schemas usage-invariants) used by Mission Control, check-usage and the sync gate. Each audit root cause, rebuilt as a builder in code, fails its invariant; the current pipeline keeps them all.

stations.title: Real path, synthetic sessions
stations.description: Mission Control from source and the built CLI against a capture portal, with otel-hook-shaped OTLP and a Claude transcript: main, plain worktree, slot, main to worktree mid-session, two parallel worktrees, a session in two repositories, a nested repository, a relaunched slot, a retried request, one session across repositories (A main, a slot in B, back to A), and resend / --full resend. The invariants hold on Mission Control and on the captured usage[], and each request lands in the place it happened.

extraStages.description: S0 — usage invariants and one regression per audit root cause
S1 — Mission Control from source, har control sync, capture portal: invariants on the shipped usage (no Docker)

traveler.note: Findings on real data go on FE-2058.

prototypeNotes: S1 needs node, git and control/node_modules; no Docker, no model, no network beyond 127.0.0.1.
Run the checker on any Mission Control: har control check-usage [--repo <path>] [--json].
